newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's ASX sees global role in mineral stocks.
newsitem.headline: Australia's ASX sees global role in mineral stocks.

text.p: Australia's best chance of winning a role in global share trading lay in the mineral resources sector, Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) managing director Richard Humphry said on Monday.

The ASX was working to make Australia a centre for mineral resource stocks, but was looking at a timescale of a decade rather than a year and would need the help of goverment, brokers, fund managers and industry, Humphry said.
"Achieving the goal may well be dependent on tax and regulatory changes as well, and possibly changes in the ASX's rules," he said in an address to the Sydney Mining Club.
"If it can be achieved, however, it would have very significant national benefits, not just benefits for the resources sector."
Humphry said Australia's stock market, while the eleventh largest national market in the world, accounted for only 1.5 percent of total capitalisation of markets in the developed world.
"And this percentage is likely to decline with the rapid growth of many emerging stock markets," he added.
However, Australia accounted for 28 percent of world capitalisation of mineral resources stocks, excluding petroleum and precious metals, and had 14 percent of world gold shares.
Australia also had a competitive advantage in areas ranging from research and analysis to accounting and geology.
Humphry said the ASX recently sponsored the annual conference of the Indonesia-Australia Business Council in Indonesia and gave a presentation on the mining sector.
"Since the conference, there has been evidence of interest in listing in Australia among Indonesian resources companies, which is what we are looking for," he said.
To further the ambition, however, Australia needed to become an acknowledged leader in all aspects of the resources industry.
